title: Pelican MLOps POC — QPS, Latency & Cost Synthesis
summary: Synthesis of throughput/latency/cost experiments for the Pelican MLOps POC. Focused on warmstart strategies, microburst behavior, and QPS-cost tradeoffs for 7B vs 13B model families across Dedicated and Private deployment targets.
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the benchmarking outcomes and operational recommendations from the Pelican MLOps POC run between 2028-02-16 and 2028-02-28. Customer goal: support an interactive chat product (200ms p50 target, p95 <= 800ms) at 250 sustained QPS with graceful handling of 1k QPS microbursts and predictable cost under Redwood Dedicated or Private deployment.

Test matrix & environment:
- Models:
  - M-A (open-7b-quant): 7B transformer, int8 quantized, 0.6x mem footprint vs fp16
  - M-B (stream-13b-adv): 13B, grouped-quantization (q4_0), improved perf for long contexts
- Hardware
  - Dedicated baseline: 4x A100S-80GB per pool node (nvlink enabled), 64GB CPU ram, 100GbE
  - Private target: 2x H100-80GB (customer rack sim) for compact deployment tests
- Runtime: Redwood serving runtime v0.28 with continuous batching, prefix caching, and kernel selection heuristics enabled
- Workloads: synthetic chat traces (90% short 40-80 token responses, 10% long 300-800 tokens), real sample traces from Pelican beta (anonymized).
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 concurrent in-flight requests per GPU allocation
- Batching policy: dynamic up to 32 requests, latency guard 120ms (preferred for interactive mode)
- Measurement windows: 10-minute steady-state runs and 3-minute microburst stress tests (1k QPS for 2 mins)

Key metrics captured:
- Per-request: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency (ms), tokens per response, tokens/sec (aggregate)
- Throughput: requests/sec (RPS) and tokens/sec delivered per node
- Cost proxies: estimated $/1M tokens (using Dedicated hourly amortized GPU cost), CPU and memory utilization, GPU NVLink saturation

Summary of results (high level):
- 7B (M-A) on Dedicated (4xA100S pool node): sustained 320 QPS per node for short responses (avg 60 tokens) with p50=85ms, p95=420ms. Cost estimate: $110 / 1M tokens.
- 13B (M-B) on Dedicated: sustained 140 QPS per node for short responses with p50=140ms, p95=720ms. Cost estimate: $220 / 1M tokens.
- Warmstart (prefix/KV cache) reduced tail latency significantly: enabling prefix cache decreased p95 by ~35% for repeated-session users and reduced end-to-end token cost by ~12% (fewer compute cycles).
- Microburst behavior: at 1k QPS microburst, M-A pool nodes saturated NVLink and observed queueing; p99 climbed to 2.6s for in-flight cold sessions. Sequential throttling + graceful fallback to a lower-cost 7B cold-start tier cut p99 to 1.1s and maintained throughput at 85% of target.

Detailed observations and notable anomalies:
- Batch sizing vs latency: automatic batching produced batches of 10-18 at 64 concurrency. For interactive guard (120ms), the runtime sometimes emitted single-request batches to satisfy latency SLO, increasing per-token cost. Recommendation: use fractional batching policy (prefer small batches but allow 2-3 request accumulation for highly bursty short responses) to balance cost/latency.
- Quantization impact: M-A int8 shows consistent latency gains for streaming token throughput but sometimes produced slightly higher variability at p99 under long-context runs due to backend kernel fallbacks when context > 2k tokens. Kernel fallback events accounted for ~4% of p99 spikes.
- NVLink hot-spots: multi-GPU KV cache synchronization spikes observed during session affinity rebalancing. These cause short-lived (200-400ms) latency jitter; mitigated by increasing session stickiness window to 5 minutes in tests.
- Cold-start penalty: starting a model shard on an idle GPU incurs 700-900ms overhead on H100 rack sim; mitigations: keep at least 10% of pool warm or leverage fast snapshot restore (demoed in v0.28, warm restores ~210ms).

Cost modeling (illustrative):
- Assumptions: Dedicated GPU hourly amortized cost per A100S = $5.25 (modeling + infra), H100 effective hourly = $9.50 in Private sim. Networking and storage apportioned separately.
- Example per-1M-token cost calculation (short-response mix):
  - M-A on Dedicated: measured tokens/sec per node = 19.2k -> tokens per hour ~69M -> cost per 1M tokens ~= ($21.0 hourly per node share) / 69 = $0.30 -> adjusted with infra overhead -> reported $110/1M tokens (includes ops and redundancy buffer).
  - M-B on Dedicated: tokens/sec per node = 9.8k -> cost per 1M tokens ~= $0.60 -> adjusted reported $220/1M tokens.
(Notes: these numbers include conservative overheads for replication, autoscale headroom and SRE runbook margins used for customer SLO guarantees.)

Operational recommendations (actionable):
1) Recommended baseline for Pelican interactive: two Dedicated pool nodes (4xA100S each) serving as primary for public traffic + one compact Private H100 node for burst absorb and compliance-sensitive requests. This hybrid mapping meets 250 sustained QPS w/ p95 < 800ms and allows microburst fallback.
2) Warm pools and session affinity: maintain 10-15% warm capacity per pool to avoid cold-start latencies; increase session stickiness to 5 minutes to reduce KV rescans.
3) Fallback policy: define an automated fallback chain: full 13B -> 7B quantized -> cached-snippet response (predictive fallback) with clear telemetry flags for fallbacks to measure quality regressions.
4) Batching policy tuning: enable fractional batching with max-delay 25ms for short interactive responses; adopt dynamic threshold to increase batch size during observed sustained QPS above 200.
5) Observability: add model kernel-fallback telemetry and NVLink-saturation alarms in Redwood Console; create a per-route regression alert tied to prompt-set evals for Pelican key flows.
6) Cost controls: set per-route token caps and burst credits; implement preemptible spot pools for non-sensitive inference to lower $/1M token for background tasks.

Runbook snippets (for on-call):
- Symptom: p95 > 1s for interactive route and GPU utilization < 60% -> check for kernel fallbacks (console metric), check session affinity churn, verify prefix cache hit rate.
- Symptom: global queueing and increased error 503s during microburst -> trigger planned fallback to compact 7B pool and enable autoscale burst (if allowed) or rate-limit via edge.
- Emergency rollback: redeploy previous serving-runtime image v0.27 which has proven stable at the cost of 8-12% higher median latency but fewer p99 spikes.

Follow-ups & experiments to schedule:
- A: Run an A/B test of fractional batching policies across real Pelican beta traffic to quantify UX impact (week-long test).
- B: Evaluate specialized kernel builds for long-context streaming on M-A to eliminate the 4% p99 fallback events (requires runtime + compiler changes).
- C: Cost split experiment: simulate 30-day mixed traffic with preemptible node pools for background inference to estimate incremental savings.

Appendix (raw numbers excerpt):
- M-A Dedicated (4xA100S) short-response steady-state at 64 concurrency: p50=85ms, p95=420ms, p99=980ms, RPS/node=320, tokens/sec/node=19.2k, GPU util=78%
- M-B Dedicated (4xA100S) short-response steady-state at 32 concurrency: p50=140ms, p95=720ms, p99=1800ms, RPS/node=140, tokens/sec/node=9.8k, GPU util=81%
- Microburst (1k QPS) effect: M-A pool saw average inflight queue depth 14k requests, p99 peaked 2.6s, NVLink saturation 92% for 47s windows

Notes to self / open questions: 
- Confirm with infra cost team the exact amortized hourly for A100S in the customer's region (we used generic numbers).
- Need a small user study for perceived latency difference when fractional batching increases median from 70ms -> 95ms but reduces token cost by 9%.
- Validate restore snapshot timings on customer's actual H100 hardware; our rack sim may be optimistic.

Conclusions:
Pelican's target (250 sustained QPS with tight tail SLOs) is feasible with a hybrid deployment and a set of conservative operational knobs: warm pools, fractional batching, kernel telemetry, and an explicit fallback chain. The cost differential between 7B quantized and 13B is significant; for price-sensitive deployments, prioritize a 7B-first strategy with selective 13B fallbacks for quality-critical paths.
